$why: Run through .bench/design-check.sh, which starts a fresh Bench on its own data folder with the fake SDK, seeds it (.bench/design-check.seed.mjs) and fills the {project}/{task}/{taskSession}/{session}/{emptyProject} ids in these routes. grid 4 is Design.md's Space decision. bodyPx 11 is Design.md's Type decision: --text-xs is the smallest step of the scale and is deliberate chrome (counts, badges), so 11 is the floor this project sets itself; the defects it catches are the off-scale 10px/12px literals that belong to no step. Both are the project's own recorded numbers, not exemptions for this app.
$ignoreWhy: `.xterm` is the vendored emulator (web/components/terminal.mjs, xterm.js). It writes its own 256-colour DOM the moment it opens - the `xterm-fg-*`/`xterm-bg-*` palette classes and its scrollbar slider - and those are a library's values, not Bench's components, so the tokens, target and semantics rules have nothing of Bench's to judge in there. `xterm.css` is the same library's stylesheet: terminal.mjs injects the <link> into the head when an emulator first boots, so it is linked rather than written inside the widget and the `ownerNode` subtree test cannot see it - naming the file is what skips it. Bench's part of the terminal is outside both and still checked: .terminal-frame, .terminal-bar, .terminal-key and the box around the emulator. The one thing inside that is Bench's to get right is the cursor blink, and that is fixed in terminal.mjs rather than left to the gate: cursorBlink is off under prefers-reduced-motion.
